historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved the Phase I plans of Satoru Nishita, of CHNMB Associates, for restoring Huntington Falls at Stow Lake.
Huntington Falls at Stow Lake, restored under a contract with Rock & Waterscape Systems, Inc., was dedicated, as the general manager reported to the Recreation and Park Commission in June 1984.
The Board of Park Commissioners gave up the boating concession at Stow Lake and ordered the boathouse demolished at once.

Recording the death of their president W. W. Stow, the Park Commissioners told how the lake that bears his name began as a reservoir on the east side of Strawberry Hill, badly needed in case the pumps failed, and was made an ornamental lake at his instance as well, with a pipe from the Almshouse artesian well feeding it without pumping.

The lake around Strawberry Hill was finished as a reservoir, holding twenty to twenty-five million gallons high enough to irrigate five-sixths of the park by gravity; the hill, now an island, was reached from the northeast over the concrete Roman bridge and from the southwest by a stone footbridge added because so many people walked out to the lake, and carriages could drive about three-quarters of the way around it.

The grading of the first section of the lake, east of Strawberry Hill, let by contract at 8½ cents a cubic yard, was finished in February 1892; its bed and banks were sealed with ten inches of tamped clay under three inches of rolled rock, and the water held. The second section, north of the hill, was graded, and the whole ring around the hill was under contract.
